job.style: a comparison of two related ideas

passage: In our daily lives, we encounter media and advertisements everywhere, from television screens to social media feeds. Many people assume that a famous brand name automatically guarantees superior quality compared to unbranded items, but this is often just a result of expensive marketing campaigns designed to create a specific image. Similarly, we often see advertisements that seem to simply inform us about new products. However, the primary goal of these ads is to persuade us to spend money, rather than just providing neutral information. When we watch news channels, it is easy to think that an independent channel always presents the absolute truth. In reality, all media outlets, whether independent or government-funded, make choices about which stories to cover and how to frame them. These choices are influenced by their own perspectives and financial interests. Because the media decides which issues to highlight, they play a powerful role in setting the public agenda. It is a mistake to believe everything they report simply because it is being shown on a screen. Instead, a responsible citizen must analyze different sources to understand the full picture, as no single report can be considered perfectly balanced or entirely objective.

items.evidence: Many people assume that a famous brand name automatically guarantees superior quality compared to unbranded items, but this is often just a result of expensive marketing campaigns designed to create a specific image.
items.q: Two soaps look alike, but the famous one costs far more. What is the likely reason?
options: Much of the price pays for marketing
It is always made with better ingredients
Unbranded goods are never tested at all
Its advertisement proves it is the best
items.explain: A famous brand often comes from costly marketing campaigns that build an image, not from better quality.

wrong.why: thinks expensive brands are always better quality
assumes unbranded goods must be unsafe
thinks a liked ad proves the brand is best

items.evidence: However, the primary goal of these ads is to persuade us to spend money, rather than just providing neutral information.
items.q: A new phone advertisement lists its features. Why does the company show it?
options: To persuade people to buy the phone
To give neutral facts about new products
To help people compare all phones fairly
To tell people what is important today
items.explain: The main goal of ads is to persuade us to spend money, not just to give neutral information.

wrong.why: thinks ads only inform about new products
mixes ads up with the news agenda

items.evidence: In reality, all media outlets, whether independent or government-funded, make choices about which stories to cover and how to frame them.
items.q: An independent channel shows only some stories about a city. What does this show?
options: It chose which stories to cover
It is showing the absolute truth
It must be supporting the government
It has shown every story of the city
items.explain: Every outlet, even an independent one, chooses which stories to cover and how to frame them.

wrong.why: thinks independent channels tell the absolute truth
thinks media should always back the government

items.evidence: Because the media decides which issues to highlight, they play a powerful role in setting the public agenda.
items.q: How does the media shape what citizens think is important?
options: By choosing which issues it highlights
By telling us only proven true facts
By letting citizens decide every headline
By giving equal time to every opinion
items.explain: Media decides which issues to highlight, so it sets the public agenda; this does not make everything it shows true.

wrong.why: thinks whatever media highlights must be true
thinks balance means equal time for all views
